answer:
The naval figure is **Admiral Edward Montagu, later 1st Earl of Sandwich**.  
Samuel Pepys mentions Montagu in every one of his December diary entries from 1660‑1667, but he does not mention him in the December 1668 entries.  

Source: Facebook post “Pepys Diary December Naval Figure Mentioned Every December Except December 1668” – https://www.facebook.com/fb-answers/pepys-diary-december-naval-figure-mentioned-every-december-except-december-1668/

### Page note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Montagu,_1st_Earl_of_Sandwich
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
**Page:** Edward Montagu, 1st Earl of Sandwich – Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Montagu,_1st_Earl_of_Sandwich)  

**Evidence**  
- **Entity:** Edward Montagu, 1st Earl of Sandwich  
  - Born: 27 July 1625 (Barnwell, Northamptonshire, England)  
  - Died: 28 May 1672 (Sole Bay, Suffolk, England) – age 46  
  - Resting place: Westminster Abbey  
  - Spouse: Jemimah Crew (m. 1642)  
  - Children: 10 (including Edward, Sidney, John)  
  - Parents: Sir Sidney Montagu and Paulina Pepys  
  - Occupation: Army and naval officer, diplomat  
  - Military service: General at sea (1656–1660), Admiral of the narrow seas (1660), Vice‑Admiral of the Blue (1672)  

- **Entity:** Samuel Pepys  
  - Cousin to Edward Montagu on his mother’s side (John Pepys, father of Samuel)  
  - Diary provides a detailed primary source of Sandwich’s career in the 1660s.  

- **Roles held by Montagu (selected list):**  
  - Ambassador to Portugal (1661–1662)  
  - Ambassador to Spain (1666)  
  - General at sea (1656–1660)  
  - Admiral of the narrow seas (1660–1671)  
  - Vice‑Admiral of the Blue (1672)  

- **Court offices table (excerpt):**  
  | Office | Years | Notes |
  |---|---|---|
  | **English Interregnum – Master of the Great Wardrobe** | 1660–1671 | Succeeded by Sir Ralph Montagu |
  | **Lord Lieutenant of Huntingdonshire** | 1660–1671 | Joint with The 2nd Earl of Manchester |
  | **Custos Rotulorum of Huntingdonshire** | 1660–1672 |  |
  | **Ambassador to Spain** | 1666 | Succeeded by Robert Spencer, 2nd Earl of Sunderland |
  | **Earl of Sandwich** | 1660–1672 |  |

- **Other relevant facts:**  
  - Montagu commanded a naval squadron during the Second Anglo‑Dutch War (1665–1667).  
  - He was involved in the Treaty of Madrid (1667) and the Treaty of Lisbon (1668).  
  - Montagu was killed in the Battle of Solebay (28 May 1672).

- The specific naval figure referenced in Samuel Pepys’s diary in every December except December 1668.  
- Any direct mention of “December” entries or a list of names appearing in those entries.
